summary:
I've been rewriting how my home server backs itself up — nightly jobs had been failing silently for two and a half months because a mount-point check written for the old hardware layout no longer matched the new disk. Fixed it and then went further: a deadman check that pings me on Telegram if a backup goes missing or comes back too small, and a full host-state snapshot (SQLite databases, systemd units, env files) so the whole box could be rebuilt from scratch, not just the databases. I ran a real restore drill against a scratch Postgres instance to prove the dump actually restores, not just that the file exists.

BudgetTracker, my personal finance tracker, now exposes its own data to my home agent (Hermes-Agent) through a set of read-only MCP tools — eleven of them, scoped so each API key only sees the accounts it's allowed to. The interesting part was building a daily spending briefing off it: yesterday's total, today's per-account breakdown, and a 14-day run-rate forecast, computed in SQL so the numbers are deterministic and a local model just phrases the summary in a sentence.

I run a couple of GPU-backed services (image generation, a local chat model) off a single shared card, which meant building a small broker (Switchboard) that queues and evicts jobs so they don't collide on VRAM. The model that answers Hermes-Agent's messages used to take minutes to respond after being idle, because reloading its 20K-token context from scratch through the slow path was expensive. Fixed it by saving and restoring its key-value cache to disk on eviction instead of recomputing it, plus a keep-warm ping every few minutes during the day.

On the side, I've been building a Japanese-learning app for myself, mostly as an excuse to think hard about what "correct" content actually means when an LLM is involved. The most useful pattern I keep re-learning: a test can pass and still be checking nothing, because the thing it was meant to guard against moved to a different file, or the population it measures shrank quietly while the ratio stayed green. I've started writing tests that assert the population itself is non-empty before trusting the rate built on top of it.

highlights.oneLiner: Rebuilt backup pipeline: deadman alerts, full host-state snapshot, verified restore drill
Added read-only MCP tools + SQL-driven daily spending briefing for the home agent
GPU broker now saves/restores model KV cache to fix multi-minute cold-start latency
